title: Observational study in Wilson disease patients treated with Trientine as part of routine clinical care, with evaluation of routinely available microbiome and autophagy-related biomarkers
summary:
Wilson disease is a rare inherited disorder in which copper accumulates in the body because of impaired copper metabolism. This can cause damage, particularly to the liver and nervous system. Trientine is a medication that helps remove excess copper from the body.

The WIDIMI study aims to improve our understanding of the gut microbiome (the community of microorganisms living in the intestine) and certain cellular recycling processes, known as autophagy, in patients with Wilson disease receiving trientine treatment. The study will explore possible associations with copper metabolism, liver function, neurological symptoms, and the course of the disease.

Up to 120 adult patients may be included if their physicians have independently decided to prescribe or continue trientine treatment. The study will evaluate existing medical information and data collected during routine clinical care over a period of up to twelve months.

This is a purely observational study. It does not influence treatment decisions or require additional examinations or sample collection. The findings are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the biological processes involved in Wilson disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Confirmed diagnosis of Wilson disease (Leipzig/Ferenci score > 3)
Switch from D-penicillamine or zinc to trientine dihydrochloride within the previous 12 months
Availability of baseline clinical data and at least one follow-up assessment
Availability of at least one microbiome sample and one autophagy-related biomarker assessment (retrospective or prospective)
Written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete documentation of prior treatment or disease course
Missing microbiome data or autophagy-related biomarker data
Active gastrointestinal disease that may substantially affect intestinal microbiome composition
Systemic antibiotic therapy within 4 weeks prior to stool sample collection
Any other condition or circumstance that, in the opinion of the investigator, may interfere with study participation or data interpretation
